derived_geometric_facts: A support form of a symmetric slab cut at a point strictly inside the slab supports the original convex body, by a short convex-segment argument. Minimum enclosing hexagons of cuts converge to a strict critical hexagon. Their side midpoints lie on the cut boundaries. If all limiting midpoints avoided the shaved faces, locality would force the smaller hexagons to enclose the original body. Thus every supporting face contains a critical midpoint.

A normalized support form for any boundary point also supports a critical midpoint in its face. Uniqueness at that midpoint identifies the form with the side normal of a critical hexagon. Average two normalized support forms at a boundary point. A critical midpoint in the average form's supporting face attains level one for both original forms. Uniqueness at critical midpoints makes the two forms equal. Together with support existence and positive normalization, this proves a unique geometric supporting line at every boundary point, without a C1 parametrization assumption.
